relevance_note: Case report of a family carrying a TNFAIP3 variant plus a second HA20 patient: "We report a case of TNFAIP3-mediated autoinflammation manifesting as progressive neuroinflammation".
method_note: Read the whole letter, figure legends, Methods and Table E1 by hand; the JSON was assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory, with every value taken from my reading and every span checked verbatim by script. People: family 1 = proband III.1, younger sister III.2, mother II.2 (all heterozygous p.T647P per Fig 1K legend), and II.4 (affected relative who died of early-onset SLE; the paper gives no explicit relationship to the proband other than the pedigree label and no genotype, so no variant row); family 2 = a 4-year-old boy with HA20 (no label; 'unnamed person 1') and his heterozygous symptomatic father. Subject II.1 appears only as a 'family member' whose serum was used in cytokine measurement, with no stated variant testing or affection status, so given no row. III.2 and II.2 inheritance left 'not reported': II.2 is called the proband's mother; the paper does not state her relation to III.2 explicitly. The father in family 2 is described only as having 'similar clinical features from early childhood'; no specific features recorded for him. Proband age '8-year-old' is age at presentation, not onset or last evaluation, so not recorded; onset taken as choreoretinitis 'from the age of 6 months' (the paper attributed it at the time to congenital infection). Variant type and pathogenicity not stated for either variant; the opening general statement about 'loss-of-function pathogenic variants' was not applied. Recurrent fever not marked excluded from 'no history of systemic symptoms' (broader statement, not fever specifically). The boy's 'recurrent oral inflammation' was not mapped to the oral ulcers checklist item. IgG/IgA/C3 values above reference ranges in Table E1 were not recorded as features because the paper does not call them abnormal. Contradictions: the text places the brain lesions 'on the left' while the Fig 1 legend says 'right paracentral lobule'; CRP of 5 mg/L is called normal against a stated normal range of <5 mg/L (recorded as stated, normal); Table E1 hemoglobin '10 g/L (120-160 g/L)' looks like a units error and was not used.

span: empiric anti-tuberculosis treatment was started (isoniazid/rifampicin/pyrazinamide/moxifloxacin)
she received treatment with 2 mg/kg/d prednisolone, weaning to 0.5 mg/kg/d over 6 months and mycophenolate mofetil (1200 mg/m^2/d). There was no response to this treatment
Intravenous cyclophosphamide (6 doses, 500-750 mg/m^2) was then given, and prednisolone continued at a higher dose (2 mg/kg/d). There was poor response to these treatments
was started on baricitinib (6 mg/d), an oral JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor that blocks interferon signaling

This resulted in rapid clinical and radiologic improvement: 24 months later, she remains stable, with no further seizures and marked resolution of the intracerebral inflammatory lesion (Fig 1, H-J). Prednisolone was weaned off for the first time in 2 years.
